The three of us hung about in the street, passing time. Early yet, but the places around us were all taverns. No minors. Students weren't exactly the desired decoration.

But this wasn't the real pleasure district down by the bay. Most customers were uncles finished with work at the factories or building sites nearby. Paise? Not much. So the shops were simple, and the bad habits stayed within a modest budget too.

We knew plenty of the people passing. Most said hello; nobody told us off. They probably knew this wasn't a street where students would actually get into trouble.

One drunk fighting another, maximum. Peaceful place, all considered.

Lekin—

One big man wearing a white suit with a completely shameless degree of whiteness. Behind him, two fellows displaying shirts so loudly patterned you could almost hear them. A little farther back, one small man with a sickly complexion.

Four different dress decisions, one identical result. Search heaven and earth: only one group could manage such unity. Bhagwan himself must have arranged the individuality just so.

Yakuza.

Maybe they weren't quite the same species as humans.

Humans gather in random clothes, and what do you have? An untidy bunch. Bas. Put monkeys in random clothes and send them into human society, though, and suddenly the group is very easy to identify.

Toh perhaps that was it.

Not occupation: yakuza.
Species: yakuza.

Socho toh sahi. Think about it properly. They lived by making other people's lives difficult.

Public receives trouble, you receive livelihood. Beech mein social contribution kahan hai? Where exactly does the benefit to society enter?

Drinking professionally was a more believable career.

Therefore this wasn't work. They caused trouble as a biological habit. No job being performed; nature was taking its course. Haan, now it made sense.

Shove a passerby. Distribute tobacco breath continuously. Kick trash for no reason. Same as a stinkbug farting. You had to understand it that way.

Getting angry would be wrong. Humanity, highest order of life, should watch these lower creatures with warmth. Study them. Surely there was much to learn.

That was the proper conduct of an intelligent species. Full scientific attitude.

大体、考えてもみるといい。
　彼らは人に迷惑をかけることで生活している。

　それは一体どういう社会貢献なのか。
　なぜそれで生活が成立するのか。

　酒を飲み歩く職業の方がまだしも現実的である。

　つまり彼らは生物的習性として他人に迷惑をかけて
いるのであり、決して、業務として行っているのでは
ないのだ。
　そう考えれば理不尽ではない。

　彼らが通行人を突き飛ばしながら歩くのも、やたら
ヤニ臭い息を始終周囲に撒き散らすのも、意味もなく
ゴミを蹴り飛ばすのも、カメムシが屁をこくのと同様
の行為なのだ。そう考える必要がある。

　彼らの行動に腹を立ててはならない。
　霊長たる人類として、下等な生物を暖かく見守り、
研究の対象とするべきだ。きっと学ぶことは多々ある
だろう。

　それこそが、知的生物人類にふさわしい姿勢である。

I'd heard the stories.

That personality didn't collect friends. Trouble, on the other hand, followed her like an affectionate puppy. She didn't actually do bad things, but the schools of Kamakura knew her as a lone-wolf delinquent anyway.

Even Rokuhara was on her opponents' list, apparently. Not openly, of course. Ambushes or something like that, more than once, people said.

Asli baat? Only she knew whether it was true.

Just from looking at her, though—pebble coming at her, boulder coming at her, same answer. Punch it.

Muramasa《Trouble found you nicely, Mido.》
Kageaki"No. Nothing particular."
Muramasa《Some good came out of it, perhaps. Those children seem to have detached themselves.》
Kageaki"Yes."
Kageaki"..."
Muramasa《Mido? Kya hua? Something troubling you?》
Kageaki"A little. The soldier-ant parasite you encountered yesterday..."
Muramasa《Haan.》
Kageaki"If it has been given an 'egg,' knowing about us would be no surprise. Initially I judged that it had appeared to target you, but—"
Muramasa《Ab otherwise? You think not?》
Kageaki"The students may have been its targets throughout. Encountering and fighting you, only something that happened along the way. I cannot exclude that."
Muramasa《...Haan. That was the danger I was following them to watch for in the first place.》
Kageaki"Enemy is a parasite, therefore that possibility need not be considered. Perhaps I arrived at that too quickly."
Muramasa《Matlab, before and now, this parasite wants to abduct boys and girls only? Nothing to do with us?》
Kageaki"Possible. Thinking back, that one more often than not told the parasites almost nothing."
Muramasa《Some didn't even know they had a parasite inside them...》
Kageaki"Yes. So taking our eyes completely off those three students is not safe. That is my conclusion."
Muramasa《Toh... divide the work?》
Kageaki"We will have to."
Muramasa《Understood...》
